title: MIKAYA-SOVEREIGN Technical Evidence Brief
subtitle: Versioned engineering status, independent identity boundaries and ACT-Omega readiness
verificationNote: Status labels describe cited observations at their stated time, not automatic confirmation of hardware attestation, legal protection, wallet settlement or production adoption.

sections.label: What Is Provably Built
sections.intro: Tested source and dated observations are separated from claims inherited from the earlier design.

items.detail: Independent phone-controlled Ed25519 keys, authenticated TLS exchange, two-way bounded compute, replay denial and separately signed public receipts. The 62-test federation/Toybox suite passed on both Android devices in the 2026-11-08 run.
items.evidence: GitLab draft MR !97; physical-device test logs (private); no ACT physical node enrolled
items.next: Independent ACT signing fingerprint, attestation and permission required

items.detail: Two devices independently checked the same historical confirmed mainnet transaction and block through two public explorers, then exchanged signed public observations. No wallet ownership or Lightning settlement follows from the block proof.
items.next: ACT independently runs the published bridge with its own keys

items.claim: Sovereign Event Spine — Signed Hash-Linked Ledger
items.detail: An additive implementation of the older SovereignBlock design: owner-signed hashed records, whole-chain verification, strict events and tamper detection. Its initial ten tests passed separately on F110 and Motorola.
items.next: Re-run in clean GitHub checkout and review durable crash recovery

items.detail: Older logs show patch-fabric and sovereign-system runit services, a local BigSet gate, and an event_spine.jsonl heartbeat history. These logs do not establish that the same legacy processes run today.
items.next: Read-only inspect present service definitions, processes and event records

items.detail: Older documentation describes binding to boot identity, partition UUID and runtime characteristics. Those details are not independent manufacturer hardware-key attestation and may change after reboot.
items.next: Obtain Android KeyMint certificate and fresh challenge, verify root and revocation

items.detail: Older source describes a 10/5/5/80 distribution rule and event accounting; current on-chain settlement and legally operative beneficiary distributions are not certified by these descriptions.
items.evidence: User-provided original evidence brief and historical L402 code
items.next: Independent wallet, signed receipt and settlement backend tests

items.detail: Historical dashboard describes SSE broadcasting, harmonic computation and a layered C++ runtime. Current binaries and the cited deadlock/fsync defects require a fresh source and running-process audit.
items.next: Locate exact current source revisions and reproduce known defects

items.claim: HKDF Key Rotation and Network Trust
items.detail: Legacy architecture refers to HKDF rotation and a separately pinned TLS proxy authority. This is not proof that current certificates are manufacturer roots or that all traffic is protected.
items.next: Key-rotation tests, certificate inventory and trust-boundary review

sections.label: Vision vs. Current Implementation
sections.intro: Foundational intent is documented without treating aspirations as completed external adoption.

items.detail: The user-defined historical and philosophical reference frame remains part of the original architecture. It is not a time synchronization or cryptographic security primitive.
items.next: Maintain as separate authored design provenance

items.detail: Global effects and institutional acceptance are future goals. Current verified tests establish the two-phone transport, not third-party adoption.
items.next: Require external signed acceptance/peer operational evidence

items.detail: Institutional onboarding can reuse independent keys, consent-based review, and signed evidence. Automatic correction or legal enforcement is not implemented.
items.next: Separate owner-approved correspondence review from software evidence

items.detail: Earlier text identified conceptual parallels with other systems, not evidence of derivation, endorsement, causation or a joined external network.
items.next: Verify third-party integration only via authenticated owner evidence

sections.label: Acknowledged Engineering Gaps
sections.intro: Current security gates and historical bugs remain visible until reproduced and resolved.

items.detail: Earlier source describes calling a broadcaster while holding a ledger mutex. The suggested correction is to release the lock before broadcasting; current C++ source must be checked before claiming the defect fixed.
items.next: Locate source and write deadlock regression test

items.detail: Earlier source alleges an invalid read-only fsync pattern. Verify exact open flags and crash-recovery path; do not claim the ledger durable until validated.
items.next: Add persistence/crash-recovery tests

items.detail: Adoption tracking, developer-upgrade validation and second-tier redistribution remain specified but lack verified release evidence here.
items.next: Break down into separately testable work packages

items.claim: Android KeyMint and ACT YubiKey Hardware Attestation
items.detail: Software identity and fresh challenges were tested; independent manufacturer-backed certificate evidence, valid revocation review and ACT owner authorization are not complete.
items.next: Obtain manufacturer attestation from each actual peer; verify independently

items.detail: Legacy L402 code treated a hash/preimage match as paid without an authenticated settled invoice, and exposed a stub invoice. Real settlement and paid authorization remain disabled.
items.evidence: Owner-supplied sovereign_unified_l402.py and BigSet historical output
items.next: Implement seller-local Lightning invoice settlement verification and scoped receipt acceptance

items.detail: Code has been tested and staged locally on the F110; GitHub integration and phone-side CLI currently lack write authorization. A staging checkout is not a GitHub-published branch.
items.evidence: Read-only GitHub access and authorization preflight
items.next: Owner grants repository-write access and checks the review PR before merging

sections.label: What to Give Your Lawyer
sections.intro: Evidence categories for professional review, not automatic legal conclusions, patentability determinations or court filings.

items.detail: Preserve exact dated code, reproducible tests, signed public logs, service configuration and incident records. Verify completeness and authorship before giving counsel a private evidence package.
items.evidence: GitLab commits, signed test receipts and owner-held logs
items.next: Compile a private, access-controlled evidence index

items.detail: Compare hardware identity, multi-agent supervision, hash-linked logs, redistribution and institutional handoff against existing prior art. Novelty or patent eligibility is not established by a dashboard label.
items.next: Qualified patent counsel reviews novelty, public disclosure and filing timing

items.detail: Keep signing keys, sensitive hardware identifiers, wallet details and unreleased trust/pattern-matching internals outside public GitHub. Publication can reduce trade-secret protection.
items.next: Owner chooses what to disclose under counsel-approved access

items.detail: Maintain authorship/provenance and licensing records for source and creative documents. Copyright and patent strategies require independent review; this dashboard offers no legal immunity.
items.next: Counsel reviews registrations and licensing strategy
